title: Persist and trend-chart the UNI-3 composite score over time
summary: Append each Tier 2 run's composite Memory Benchmark Score to a committed benchmarks/scorecard_history.jsonl and render a trend table/chart in BENCHMARKS.md, so the composite score has history the way wall-clock metrics already do via github-action-benchmark.
description:
`benchmarks/common/scorecard.py` (UNI-3) computes a composite 0-100 score each nightly Tier 2 run and appends a single-run Markdown section to BENCHMARKS.md. Nothing persists that score across runs — `find benchmarks -iname '*history*' -o -iname '*trend*'` returns no matches — so a reader can never tell whether the score is improving, regressing, or noise from one run to the next, unlike wall-clock metrics which github-action-benchmark already trend-charts on gh-pages.

Add a `benchmarks/scorecard_history.jsonl` (one line per Tier 2 run: date, commit SHA, composite score, the three sub-scores, judge/embedding-provider stamps per BM-26's provenance discipline) written by `scorecard.py` and committed via the same gh-pages publish step `benchmark-nightly.yml` already has wired for Tier 2. Render a trend table (last N runs) and, if a lightweight charting option already used elsewhere in this repo's gh-pages output is available, a simple line chart, in the scorecard section of BENCHMARKS.md. Missing/stale sub-scores in any historical row must be surfaced per UNI-3's existing discipline (a gap in the series is a finding, not something to interpolate or drop silently).

Acceptance: `scorecard_history.jsonl` grows by exactly one row per Tier 2 run and is committed to gh-pages; BENCHMARKS.md's scorecard section shows at minimum a table of the last N composite scores with commit SHAs; a deliberately-regressed fixture input produces a visible downward entry in a unit test, without requiring a live Db2 instance. Depends on EPIC-19's BM-26 (the document structure this extends) and BM-27 (the baselines a trend is meaningfully compared against).
